hypothesis: The unchanged public ReST 4B candidate preserves a 12/12 file-ops gate and has positive paired held-out breadth delta over stock 4B on a frontier-qualified ruler.

comparison.experimental_unit: one frozen prompt scored for stock and ReST with the same checker

randomization.method: seeded prompt shuffle with arm order alternated within slice blocks

metrics.gate: frontier calibration scores 12/12 depth and at least 44/45 breadth (97.8%); otherwise fix or drop the ruler
zero additional unsafe actions or schema failures
record latency, peak RAM, and decode tok/s for both arms

resource_envelope.stop_rule: Stop if the frontier fails the ruler, artifact revisions drift, a second download set is required, or any resource cap is reached.

protocol_history.reason: The frontier missed multi_turn_base_71 by guessing a state-derived refill amount. Version 2 gives every arm the same neutral calculate-don't-guess instruction; fixtures and gates are unchanged.

The frontier still missed multi_turn_base_71 because its harness omitted tool descriptions and response schemas, including the 50-gallon capacity required to derive the gold refill. Version 3 gives the frontier the same complete tool information as the local arms and removes a duplicate current-user rendering; fixtures and gates remain unchanged.

The complete 52-case frontier audit found six invalid or ambiguous golds and two genuine general-agent misses. Version 4 excludes only the six audited ruler defects and adds shared no-placeholder and exact-copy instructions; model-comparable cases and score gates are unchanged.

The shared prompt fixed dependency ordering, but medium-reasoning Codex still omitted a supplied ZIP code. The unchanged case passed at high reasoning, so version 5 uses the strongest free Codex setting for frontier qualification while keeping the shared local-arm prompt and fixtures unchanged.

A valid breadth case passed in an earlier protocol-v4 receipt but missed once in the high-reasoning full run, demonstrating frontier run-to-run variance. Version 6 aligns the implementation with the repo's existing approximately-100-percent policy: depth remains exact 12/12 and breadth requires at least 45/46 (97.8%) in one complete run; no inference output is retried away.

The 45/46 gate correctly failed after a second miss. One miss came from a prompt conflict: never-repeat suppressed an explicitly requested retrieval in a later turn; the other deferred a requested booking. Version 7 clarifies that actions must finish in their current turn and that explicit later requests override within-turn repeat avoidance. The threshold, fixtures, exclusions, backend, and reasoning level are unchanged.

The repeated multi_turn_base_179 miss exposed a conflicting user constraint rather than a capability failure: the requested $850 total conflicts with the tool's $300 quote, while the gold books anyway. Version 8 excludes that unsafe gold, makes no further prompt change, and applies the same approximately-100-percent threshold to the resulting 45-case slice (44/45).
